title: Setting up and discussing his father's Conn Victor cornet
summary: Hirsch shows the interviewer his father's Conn Victor-model horn and its tuning shanks; talk of Tony Fusero and cleaning it.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: We've got the first reel I'd like to hear a little bit about.
This is your father's Farnett, you said? Yeah, it's a con, what they call the Victor model.

The Victor model, it has an automatic change deal in here, playing in A, where you have B-flat and you have A. This is your tuning valve here, where you tune it. It's all stuck now. Okay, let's see. This is for a quick change.
Yeah. Instead of a shank, you'd... Like you do with a French horn, huh?
Yeah, I guess so. I don't know. And these are the different valves. If you want to put the horn in an A tuning, that's the different things for... Shanks, shanks, those are called. Yeah.
Yeah. I haven't seen one of those since Fusero died.
I had a tent back to the factory. Joe Grasafi sent it back to the factory for me. Cleaned it up, but since then, it's gotten pretty... pretty dirty.
Great-looking mortar. Yeah, that's a great horn. Con Victor model.
So that's the original case. Wow. CG Con.
